concept.text: A proof that no three positive integers a, b and c satisfy a^n + b^n = c^n for any integer n greater than 2. Proved by Andrew Wiles, with Richard Taylor, in 1995. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem
page.definition: A proof that aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ has no solutions in positive integers a, b and c for any integer n>2. Andrew Wiles established the theorem in 1995, using a companion paper written with Richard Taylor.

goal.need: Computations ruled out solutions for every odd prime exponent below four million. Raising that bound would always leave larger primes unexamined. A general proof settles the question for all of them. The method also gave number theorists a way to relate elliptic curves to modular forms. Extending it beyond semistable curves established that relationship for every elliptic curve over the rational numbers.

completion.title: A proof excludes positive integer solutions to aⁿ + bⁿ = cⁿ for every integer n > 2.
completion.criterion: A complete proof establishes aⁿ + bⁿ ≠ cⁿ for all positive integers a, b, c and every integer n ≥ 3. Equivalently, it suffices to prove the assertion for n = 4 and every odd prime exponent. Acceptance after mathematical scrutiny or verification of the full statement in a proof assistant confirms the result.
completion.set_by: Mathematical community convention, expressed in the 1816 prize problem and in mathlib’s definition of FermatLastTheorem.
completion.threshold_quote: `a ^ n + b ^ n = c ^ n` has no nontrivial natural solution when `n ≥ 3`.
completion.basis: Andrew Wiles’s paper and the companion paper by Richard Taylor and Wiles appeared in May 1995. Göttingen’s prize rules allowed publication in a periodical, monograph or book and required at least two years before an award. Wiles received the Wolfskehl Prize on 27 June 1997. In 2026, Lean checked a complete formalization of the theorem against mathlib’s statement using only Lean’s three standard axioms.

milestones.title: The equation x⁴ + y⁴ = u² is proved to have no positive integer solutions.
milestones.criterion: A proof excludes all positive integers x, y, u satisfying x⁴ + y⁴ = u². Taking u = z² gives the exponent-four case.
milestones.set_by: Mathematical community convention: Fermat’s infinite-descent theorem, reproduced with proof by Arne B. Sletsjøe for the Abel Prize.
milestones.threshold_quote: has no solution among the positive integers.

milestones.title: Modularity of semistable elliptic curves over Q is proved to imply Fermat’s Last Theorem.
milestones.criterion: Show that a primitive positive integer solution to aᵖ + bᵖ = cᵖ for a prime p ≥ 5 would yield a semistable elliptic curve over ℚ that is not modular. With the cases n = 3 and n = 4, this makes modularity of every semistable elliptic curve over ℚ sufficient for Fermat’s Last Theorem.
milestones.set_by: Ribet’s level-lowering theorem and its application to the Frey curve, in the semistable formulation given by Wiles.
milestones.threshold_quote:
Ribet's result only requires one to prove the conjecture
 for semistable elliptic curves in order to deduce Fermat's Last Theorem.

milestones.title: Every semistable elliptic curve over the rational numbers is proved to be modular.
milestones.criterion: For every elliptic curve E over ℚ with good or multiplicative reduction at every prime, prove that there is a positive integer N and a nonconstant map X₀(N) → E defined over ℚ. The reduction condition is semistability. The map from the modular curve X₀(N) gives a modular parametrization of E.
milestones.set_by: Mathematical community convention: the semistable case of the Shimura–Taniyama modularity conjecture, established as Theorem 0.4 in Wiles’s 1995 paper.
milestones.threshold_quote: Suppose that E is a semistable elliptic curve defined over Q. Then E is modular.

milestones.title: Fermat’s Last Theorem is proved for every odd regular prime exponent.
milestones.criterion: For every odd prime p that does not divide the class number of ℚ(ζₚ), a proof excludes all positive integer solutions to aᵖ + bᵖ = cᵖ. Here ζₚ is a primitive pth root of unity, and the class number is the number of ideal classes in that field.
milestones.set_by: Kummer’s regular-prime theorem, stated as flt_regular in Annals of Formalized Mathematics.
milestones.threshold_quote:
theorem flt_regular {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hreg : IsRegularPrime p) (hodd : p ≠ 2) :
  FermatLastTheoremFor p

milestones.title: A proof excludes all positive integer solutions to x³ + y³ = z³.
milestones.criterion: For all positive integers x, y, z, prove x³ + y³ ≠ z³. This also covers every positive multiple n = 3k by applying the cubic assertion to xᵏ, yᵏ and zᵏ.
milestones.set_by: The classical cubic case, stated as fermat-3 in the Archive of Formal Proofs.
